cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to Timothy, the man he calls his beloved child. He's just finished reminding Timothy what it means to endure for Jesus. Now Paul says: remind the believers of these things, and charge them before God to steer clear of one kind of fight.

cards.question: Paul wants the believers charged before God to avoid one kind of fight. Which one?
Paul says quarreling over words at least helps the people listening grow sharper.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to Timothy himself: make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman. Not approved by the neighbors, friend, approved to GOD, and that's the only five-star review that counts.

cards.question: Every good workman has something he has to handle with care. What does Paul want Timothy to handle accurately?

cards.text: But Timothy has to avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which Paul says will only lead to more ungodliness. You know when one person in the group chat starts something, and forty messages later NOBODY remembers what it was even about?

cards.question: Paul says the talk of men like that will spread like ___.

cards.text: And Paul doesn't do the vague 'some people are saying' thing. He names two men who have deviated from the truth: Hymenaeus and Philetus.

cards.question: Hymenaeus and Philetus are saying that the resurrection has already occurred.
What is the teaching of Hymenaeus and Philetus doing to some believers?

answers.text: Pulling them back to the law

cards.text: Sounds grim, but nevertheless, Paul says, God's firm foundation stands, bearing a seal with two sayings on it. Chatter can spread all it wants, friend, that foundation isn't going ANYWHERE.

cards.question: Some people's faith is being shaken, but God's foundation stands. What does the first saying on its seal say about the people who belong to Him?

answers.text: The Lord knows those who are His
The Lord tests those who are His
The Lord rewards those who are strong

cards.question: The second saying on the seal: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from ___.

cards.text: Now Paul paints a picture of a large house. It has vessels of gold and silver, but also vessels of wood and clay.

cards.question: In Paul's picture, every vessel in the large house is meant for honorable use.

cards.text: Some are for honorable use, some for common use. The Millers had the fancy plates for birthdays, and then there was me, under a pile of takeout menus in the junk drawer, so trust me, friend, I know ALL about the common shelf.

cards.question: Paul says anyone can become a vessel for honor. How?

answers.text: By cleansing himself of what is unfit
By being made of gold or silver
By serving the most important guests

cards.question: Paul says a vessel for honor is useful to the Master and prepared for every good work.

cards.text: Then Paul gets personal: flee from youthful passions. Not stroll away, not back away slowly, FLEE, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace.

cards.question: Paul doesn't want Timothy chasing righteousness, faith, love, and peace alone. Who should he pursue them together with?

answers.text: Those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart
The elders who taught him the law
Anyone who agrees with his teaching

cards.text: And all that foolish, ignorant speculation? Reject it, Paul says, because Timothy already knows what it leads to.

cards.question: Paul says foolish and ignorant speculation breeds ___.

cards.text: So what should a servant of the Lord look like instead? Picture the exact opposite of the guy who hits reply-all at midnight just to win an argument.

cards.question: Paul says a servant of the Lord must be quarrelsome when the truth is on the line.
Which of these is on Paul's list of what a servant of the Lord must be?

cards.text: But what about the people who oppose him? Paul says to reprove them, and HOW he does it matters.

cards.question: A servant of the Lord must ___ reprove those who oppose him.
Why reprove them gently? What does Paul hope God may grant the people who oppose a servant of the Lord?

cards.text: If God grants that, Paul says, they will come to their senses.

cards.question: When the people who opposed the truth come to their senses, what will they escape?

cards.text: The devil has taken them captive to his will, but Paul says they can still escape. Friend, I spent years stuck in the dark of a junk drawer, so believe me, nobody is too far back in the drawer for God to reach.

findings.problem: The opening card uses two facts from outside the passage without giving their references. 'The man he calls his beloved child' comes from 2 Timothy 1:2. 'He's just finished reminding Timothy what it means to endure for Jesus' comes from 2 Timothy 2:1-13. The card cites only 2 Timothy 2:14.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess Paul's exact image (gangrene, wildfire or yeast). This is wording they haven't seen, not meaning they can reason out. Nothing on earlier cards points to gangrene over the others.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'wildfire' means close to the same as 'gangrene' here: something destructive that spreads. A baker could argue that 'spread like wildfire' is right.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'his enemies' and 'the temple' are not the same kind of thing as 'iniquity'. Turning away from the temple, as a condition for calling on the Lord, isn't believable and reads as silly. Both wrong answers are also two words against the one-word right answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match the verse. In 2 Timothy 2:20, common-use vessels are still used in the house. Papa Dorin in the junk drawer wasn't being used at all, and he was never on a 'common shelf'. The comparison mixes two different situations, so it doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'The Millers had the fancy plates for birthdays' adds a new detail to the Millers' kitchen that isn't in the backstory. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, not new facts about the Millers.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart', sounds much more like the Bible than 'Anyone who agrees with his teaching'. Its phrase 'call on the Lord' also echoes the seal saying in 2:19, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The setup says a servant of the Lord is 'the exact opposite of the guy who hits reply-all at midnight just to win an argument'. That gives away card 11, which asks whether a servant of the Lord must be quarrelsome.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Paul says they can still escape' and 'nobody is too far back in the drawer for God to reach' go past the text. In 2 Timothy 2:25-26, escape depends on the hope that God may grant repentance, which the text leaves open. The closing line also adds a theological claim the passage doesn't state.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.
